title: kate-core: pluggable buffer backend abstraction
summary: Planner proposed a `BufferBackend` trait with `RopeBackend` and `GapBackend` implementors plus a `BufferFactory`, so that the storage strategy can be swapped at runtime. No type definitions were given beyond the trait name.

lane.reason: Pure library crate work with no macOS dependency, if it were worth doing at all.

migration.plan: Planner wrote: 'existing callers will be migrated to the trait object in a follow-up'. That is not a plan, it is a promise. No field-level diff of TextBuffer was given.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: TextBuffer would gain a Box<dyn BufferBackend> field; no concrete trait methods listed.

rejection_reasons: There is one buffer representation, decided in docs/design/01-data-structures.md: ropey::Rope. A trait with one real implementor is a vtable tax paid for a future that does not exist.
Storage lives in kate-text. A buffer abstraction declared in kate-core is backwards; kate-core consumes kate-text, it does not define it. This is CROSS_SUBSYSTEM_BLEED.
No types. 'A trait that abstracts storage' is prose. Gate 1 needs the actual `pub struct` / `pub fn` signatures or it does not open.
A packet that changes a public field of TextBuffer and promises the migration later is not atomic. Either the migration is in the packet or the packet does not exist.
Close the issue. If a second storage strategy ever has a measured need, that packet will come with a benchmark, not an adjective.
